body.statement: For any one-stratum full law \(Q\), define \(w_Q(y,1)=E_Q[q_{x,Y(0),Y(1)}^{-1}\mid Y(1)=y,Z=1]\) and \(w_Q(y,0)=E_Q[(1-q_{x,Y(0),Y(1)})^{-1}\mid Y(0)=y,Z=0]\). With Ishikawa--He--Kanamori's observed-policy-first divergence orientation and generator \(f_N\), \(Q\mapsto w_Q\) embeds every full-law ATE fiber into \(\mathcal W^{\mathrm{IHK}}_{\Gamma}(P)\), preserves its ATE, and satisfies \(\mathscr R_{\mathrm{IHK},P}(w_Q)\leq R_P(Q)\), while the unrelaxed divergence is exactly \(R_P(Q)\). The ATE slice is feasible in their Jensen--CMC program at budget \(\rho\) if and only if \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq\rho\), so \(\widetilde C^{\mathrm{IHK}}_P(\tau)\leq C_P(\tau)\) under the same odds cap and numerical budget. For \(e_x=1/2\), \(p_1=4/5\), \(p_0=1/5\), \(\Gamma=4\), and \(\tau=3/10\), the relaxed program reduces exactly to \(\min_{m_1-m_0=3/10}J(m_1,m_0)=9/91\), attained at \((m_1,m_0)=(13/20,7/20)\), whereas \(C_P(3/10)=9/70\).
body.justification: The explicit weight embedding and exact rational separation show, on the published budget scale, the quantitative price of requiring one cross-world-compatible assignment mechanism.
body.gap: IshikawaHeKanamori2026Convex, equations (10), (12), and (14), defines the unrelaxed \(f\)-divergence model and its Jensen--CMC relaxation but leaves realizability open; it does not identify the Neyman-generator embedding or this strict full-law ATE gap.
body.consumer: A sensitivity analyst avoids declaring an ATE feasible at budgets between \(9/91\) and \(9/70\) when no compatible joint assignment law exists.
